column3: The Hebrew has one question beginning “why”, followed by “and no man is with you”; BSB makes these two separate why-questions.

The Hebrew explicitly names Ahimelech the priest and repeats the matter and the command as direct royal speech; BSB condenses that speech. Meeting David is supplied in BSB’s description of the young men’s instructions.
The Hebrew names both “under your hand” and “into my hand”; BSB keeps only the first as “on hand”.
The Hebrew explicitly names David as the one answered and has singular “a woman”; BSB leaves David implicit and uses plural “women”.

The Hebrew refers to yesterday and the third day, repeats the holy vocabulary, and ends with a singular vessel; BSB condenses these expressions into customary abstinence and greater holiness on the present mission.
The Hebrew says the priest gave a “holy thing” without separately naming bread in that clause; BSB supplies “bread”.
The Hebrew names “under your hand” and “in my hand”; BSB has “on hand” and “with me”.
The Hebrew explicitly says David arose before fleeing; BSB omits this action.
The Hebrew names their eyes when describing his changed behavior and uses a singular collective hand; BSB says “before them” and plural “hands”.
